chunks: ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who dies and leaves behind his sister and his mawālī. He said:

Whenever a man leaves a blood relative, whether male or female, such as a daughter of a sister, a daughter of a daughter, a daughter of a maternal uncle, a daughter of a maternal aunt, a daughter of a paternal uncle, a daughter of a paternal aunt, or anyone more remote than them, then all the estate belongs to the blood relatives, even if they are of lower degree. The mawālī do not inherit anything along with any one of them.

Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned them, assigned for them, and informed that they have greater right in the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “And those related by blood are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah.”
And He did not mention the mawālī.

key_terms.أَوْلُوا الْأَرْحَامِ: those bound by ties of kinship
key_terms.الْمَوَالِي: freed slaves or clients connected by wala', not by blood lineage
key_terms.ذَا رَحِمٍ: a blood relative connected through kinship
key_terms.ذَوِي الْأَرْحَامِ: distant kindred or extended blood relatives who inherit by kinship
key_terms.فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: in the decree or ruling of Allah as established in revelation

ai.seo_question: Do freed slaves inherit when the deceased has surviving blood relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance: when a deceased person leaves any blood relatives from among the category of dhawi al-arham, the estate goes to them rather than to freed slaves or their affiliation-based heirs. It supports this ruling by citing the Qur'anic principle that blood relatives have greater priority over one another in the Book of Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5653 - Ali ibn Yaqteen asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who dies and leaves behind his sister and his freed slaves.
Imam (as) said: "The wealth belongs to his sister."
